prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour. Communications-Based Train Control system (CBTC) protects separation/authority/regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (regulation/recovery/incidents), Revenue Train Operator (readiness/cab/passengers), Cyber Security Officer (access/security). Operations Control Centre workflow: Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) displays positions/routes/alarms/performance; proposes holding/skip-stop/turnback/run-through using timetable variance/dwell/headway/route availability; displays action/train identities/recovery prediction before confirmation. Controller must assess passenger/downstream impacts; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice with confirmed limits/speed/start/removal condition; monitors delay/recovery margins; records incident time/train/location/passenger impact/first safe instruction. Lantern sends Crew Login Token Bundle; no vital intervention. Voice Dispatch Console cannot replace safety validation. Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved messages; Service Timetable Server supplies schedules; non-vital outputs isolated. North District Zone Controller (Marble): north/turnback/East Junction Interlocking (Falcon) approach. South District Zone Controller (Orchid): south/turnback/West Junction Interlocking approach. Controllers constrain authorities using location/occupancy/field-state, preserve separation/locking, report conflicts; transfers require ownership/overlap/receiving validation. Interlockings retain locking/release; release requires detection/point correspondence/opposing-route criteria. Authorities require proved/locked points, protected overlaps/flanks; restrictive evidence prevails; correspondence loss shortens/withdraws safely. Axle counters independently prove availability. East sends Axle Counter Reset Request; no reset with locked routes/approaches. Maple (full name unspecified) records clearance. West sends Route Release Exception List; hazards persist until exclusion; route indications distinguish delay/fault. Platform Screen Door Controller supplies closed/locked readiness, not route proof. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): authenticated/integrity-checked activation; initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout; validates authority/context/token, enforces profiles, indicates rejection/degradation; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies independent distance/speed/boundary confidence; divergence increases uncertainty/separation. Feedback checked; stale acknowledgements rejected. Train Radio Modem uses monitored Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron), sending Radio Handover Audit File; degradation retains validated authority; radio loss may require holds. Safety Data Communication Network:

New part:
S117: The Voice Dispatch Console is used when direct verbal instruction is required, and the instruction is repeated back by the Revenue Train Operator before the action is treated as accepted.
S118: The Revenue Train Operator reports train condition, cab indications, passenger issues, and any local hazard that cannot be confirmed from the control room display alone.
S119: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server provides non-vital trend data that helps the Signal Maintenance Engineer determine whether an incident has an equipment cause or an operational cause.
S120: The Signal Maintenance Engineer advises the Line Traffic Controller on equipment recovery options, but the Line Traffic Controller remains responsible for service regulation decisions during the event.
S121: The Service Timetable Server is updated only through an approved timetable change workflow, and the Line Traffic Controller verifies that the revised plan is visible before relying on it for regulation.
S122: The Passenger Information Gateway receives the operational service state needed to align platform messages and train destination information with the current regulating plan.
S123: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance uses the sample report to verify that certificate validity windows and controller clocks remain within the permitted tolerance before operational use.
S124: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance produces the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack under an approved maintenance window and records the change reference for later security audit.
S125: The Cyber Security Officer reviews certificate change records, access events, and unusual authentication failures before authorising normal operational reliance on the renewed security configuration.
S126: Authority review is performed after major incidents, degraded operations, and timetable interventions to confirm that each commanded movement remained consistent with interlocking state, controller intent, and recorded train response.
S127: This section describes the operational interfaces between the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System and station equipment that affects departures, passenger information, and dispatcher awareness.
S128: Platform equipment is treated as part of the movement-authority environment when its state can prevent a train from arriving, dwelling, or departing safely.
S129: Platform Screen Door Controller produces the Platform Door Status Snapshot at each monitored platform face for operational use by the CBTC system.
S130: The door interface reports closed, locked, bypassed, inhibited, and faulted conditions using coded states that are interpreted consistently across the line.
S131: A departure command is not considered available to the Revenue Train Operator until the relevant platform door state is compatible with the requested direction of travel.
S132: North District Zone Controller suppresses platform departure authority when the associated berth reports an unsafe door interface state.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
